sources.title: Identifying property and street information
sources.verified_claim: Government requires UPRN and USRN identifiers for property and street information systems and describes UPRN as the unique identifier for every addressable GB location.

sources.title: Access free address data using AddressBase
sources.verified_claim: Government guidance requires the UPRN standard when identifying places and explains that UPRNs support cross-referencing and reduce data-exchange errors.

sources.title: OS Open UPRN
sources.verified_claim: OS Open UPRN provides all UPRNs in AddressBase Premium with point geometries in British National Grid and latitude/longitude; point identity is not a legal parcel boundary.

sources.title: National Statistics UPRN Lookup (May 2026) (Epoch 126)
sources.verified_claim: ONS links UPRNs to administrative and statistical geographies, mostly using best-fit allocation from census output areas; the geography link is not an exact title-boundary relationship.

sources.title: Title Number and UPRN Look Up dataset - Technical specification
sources.verified_claim: HMLR links title numbers to AddressBase UPRNs only where it can establish an address relationship; not every title can therefore be assumed to have a UPRN link.

sources.title: Government Property Data Standard: GovS004-PDS010
sources.verified_claim: The government property standard stores UPRN and property boundary as distinct data elements, reinforcing that an identifier and polygon extent are separate concepts.

sources.title: National Statistics UPRN Products
sources.verified_claim: ONS describes UPRN lookup products for assigning properties to statistical geographies using point-in-polygon and best-fit methods depending on the product.

sources.title: Addresses - National Data Library
sources.verified_claim: The authoritative address collection is updated daily and links address lifecycle records using UPRN; address authority does not itself establish ownership or legal title extent.
